page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a 945 GB local disk and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the D16ads_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by its top-25% rankings in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core scores. Text processing and text generation for small LLM models (135M parameters) also rank in the top tier. However, multi-core performance, database operations, and static web serving throughput align with average middle-tier expectations. A notable performance bottleneck is identified in memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks (256MB), which ranks in the bottom 25%, and large-model (70B) LLM prompt processing, which falls into the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D16ads_v6 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads that require a mix of compute, memory, and local storage without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The inclusion of a 945 GB local disk provides high-speed temporary storage, making it highly suitable for relational databases, web serving, software compilation, and intermediate ETL processing. Conversely, it is poorly suited for large-scale LLM inference or memory-bound applications that frequently access large, uncached memory blocks.

It features 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores), 64.0 GB of RAM, and a 945 GB local disk. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance and text processing capabilities, alongside average multi-core and database execution speeds. However, it exhibits weak memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and poor performance on large-scale LLM inference. Lacking a GPU, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for balanced workloads requiring moderate local storage. It is best suited for web serving, database operations, software compilation, and small-scale machine learning tasks.
